query: What is AFFO adjusted funds from operations for a data center REIT
normalized: adjusted affo center data funds operations reit

output.content:
AFFO—**adjusted funds from operations**—is a non-GAAP cash-flow proxy used to assess a data-center REIT’s recurring earnings available after the recurring spending needed to sustain its properties and revenue base. [[1]] 

It generally starts with FFO and deducts (i) recurring capitalized maintenance expenditures, such as ongoing property improvements, leasing costs, and tenant-improvement allowances, and (ii) the effect of GAAP straight-line rent accounting. [[1]] 

For a data-center REIT, investors commonly use AFFO and AFFO per share to evaluate recurring cash-generation capacity, dividend coverage, and valuation, because it adjusts FFO for the continuing capital needs of operating data-center facilities. [[1]] 

A simplified formulation is: **AFFO = FFO − recurring maintenance/tenant/leasing capital expenditures − straight-line-rent adjustment ± company-specific recurring adjustments.** [[1]] 

Importantly, AFFO is not standardized, so the precise adjustments—and whether particular spending is classified as maintenance versus growth capex—can differ by REIT; investors should use the company’s own reconciliation and definition when comparing issuers. [[1]]
